recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

recMVdJjP2VZJyI2m.Body: Clive de Carle has spent decades researching high-quality natural health essentials, from magnesium and fulvic minerals to iodine, selenium, and vegan-sourced vitamin D. His supplements are formulated with a focus on bioavailability, so the body can actually absorb and use what you're taking rather than letting it pass through unused. It's a simple, no-nonsense approach to filling the nutritional gaps most modern diets leave behind.

rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Bio: Chance Garton is the host and producer of the Innerverse Podcast, where for over a decade he has investigated consciousness, mythology, symbolism, terrain health, and the psychosomatic language of the human body and mind. A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Name: Chance Garton
rec7Vm5QNrDbc9sdb.Role: Host of the Innerverse Podcast, biofield tuning practitioner & researcher

recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Bio: Gabriel, known on air as Slick Dissident, co-hosts InnerVerse's Vibe Rant show and is a longtime recurring guest on the podcast. He teaches occult symbolism and tarot on his YouTube channel, ranging across the Major Arcana, the esoteric Enneagram, mythology and archetype, mystic linguistics, and the symbolism hidden in popular film. He is best known for Tarot-tories, his own system mapping the 22 Major Arcana and zodiac archetypes onto the geography of the United States.
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Name: Gabe (Slick Dissident)
recBE7KwrPCyVVZMU.Role: Co-host of Vibe Rant; teacher of occult symbolism & tarot

recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Bio: Kyle Denton is a community herbalist and medicine maker from Wisconsin who founded Tippecanoe Herbs with his wife Serena Marinelli in 2015. From their Milwaukee apothecary they craft small batch remedies from locally harvested and organic herbs, working from a bio terrain philosophy that blends Ayurveda with Western herbalism. He also runs Root Radical Herbal Academy, has taught for over a decade through his annual three season class and his Milwaukee herb walks, and sees clients as the Tuning Herbalist, using tuning forks to read the biofield. His Substack and podcast, Resonature, explore the interval between vital herbalism, biofield tuning and cosmology.
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Name: Kyle Denton
recbqsYSV8FGvCA28.Role: Community herbalist, founder of Tippecanoe Herbs

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "Rituals We Were Tricked Into", "body": "Jorge says his recent run of music episodes on Third Eye Edify landed on one idea: how easy it is to trick an entire populace into rituals that are not good for us, from breakfast, coffee and tobacco to screens and the phone we cannot put down. He argues music has become one of them, with equal temperament, a 440 standard and endless covers making the notes almost inconsequential while listeners fixate on lyrics. Looping the same ten radio tracks, he says, keeps people in an adolescent mindset. Chance adds that what counts as breakfast food, and even three meals a day, may be imposed habits too."}, {"title": "All Consequent, No Antecedent", "body": "Borrowing the musical idea of antecedent and consequent phrasing, a call and its answer, Jorge says modern culture is all consequent and no antecedent: people want to read the last page of a book or watch someone else finish the video game rather than play it. Kyle notices that Rich Men North of Richmond never resolves into a chorus, so every line becomes the hook. Chance says its chord progression is the same earworm recycled across many viral pop songs."}, {"title": "Anchors, Layers and Reenacted Myths", "body": "Chance argues that movies, television and music work as a ritual reenactment of mythology, setting up subconscious agreements about archetypes like mother, father, wife, husband and partner, so that people raised on sitcoms carry those scripts into their own relationships. The conversation also turns to the NLP technique of anchoring, pairing an unusual gesture or scent with a desired state until the cue alone brings it back, and to the suggestion that mass media applies the same conditioning at scale. Layering, stories nested inside stories as in The Simpsons and Seinfeld, is described as a way to plant a message that surfaces later."}, {"title": "The Ritual Wheel Never Stands Still", "body": "Chance explains the episode title: rituals feel static, yet they are always evolving, and unless he intentionally upgrades them with better knowledge they slip and degrade. Jorge adds that people defend even stagnant rituals fiercely, because they feel private and are often all a tired wage worker has. He agrees that emotion matters as well, noting that brushing your teeth exhausted at night, without care or feeling, is a ritual done poorly. Chance closes the thread with a practical rule for creative and health habits: set the bar low, count simply showing up as a win, and remember that what you do every day is who you are."}, {"title": "Silliness as a Spell Breaker", "body": "Kyle describes his own rituals as an herbalist: tasting plants wherever he walks and thanking them out loud, and deliberately scrambling routines with his shirt on backwards or glasses upside down, which he imagines amuses the elementals behind the mundane world. Chance contrasts healthy ritual, done because it feels good, with fear driven compulsion, and suggests rituals of satisfaction like singing after meals. Gabe later confesses a happy Zippo flipping habit, a ritual from his old normal that he admits is a little OCD and loves anyway. Chance then closes sacred space on air, returning everyone's energies to their owners."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Jorge Mesa of Third Eye Edify podcast returns to catch us up on his recent research. Jorge is a lifelong musician, teacher, father, and student of the mysteries. What are the habits that make up our day to day life? What aspects of our rituals are made for us, by us? Most importantly, what do we take for granted as normal, that may have been conditioned into us by unknown forces?
